question.text: When a PMS executes transactions on behalf of clients:

answer.text: The PM can pool all HNI holdings under its own name
Each client's securities are held and traded in the client's own name/account, with client-wise segregation
The PM retains the shares in its own name

explanation.text: The Logic: Under PMS rules, the portfolio manager must not hold client securities in its own name. Client-wise segregation is required, and trading/allocation is done at the individual client level so that each client's securities sit in the client's own demat/account. The Trap: Pooling client holdings under the portfolio manager's name or retaining shares in the PM's own name breaches the segregation requirement that PMS operations must follow. Note: Treat client-name and segregation as the load-bearing point. The specific subscription mechanism used at the issue level is a separate operational matter and should only be cited when the source page actually supports it.
